resourcePath.description:
Per-operation JSON path to the resource collection in each
response.  Outer-array length MUST match ``requestType``
length: 1 entry for single-op imports, N entries for an
N-operation composite import (duplicate the value when
operations agree).  See the ``response`` object docs
above for the full positional-array contract.

Required when ``batchSize > 1`` because the platform needs
to know where the array of result records lives inside the
response envelope.  When the API returns a bare array at
the top level, leave this field unset.

Each entry is a DOT-PATH STRING (e.g. ``"data.results"``,
``"items"``) — do NOT split paths into segments across
array elements.

resourceIdPath.description:
Per-operation JSON path to the unique ID field within each
record in the response.  Outer-array length MUST match
``requestType`` length — duplicate the value when both
operations agree (the common case) rather than collapsing
to a 1-entry array.

Each entry is a DOT-PATH STRING, or null for an operation
with no ID path configured. When not specified, the platform
looks for standard `id` or `_id` fields automatically.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Common LLM mistake:
splitting a single dot-path like ``"data.id"`` into array segments ``["data",
"id"]`` — DO NOT do this.
See the ``response`` object docs above.

successPath.description:
Per-operation JSON path to a field that indicates whether
the API call succeeded.  Outer-array length MUST match
``requestType`` length — duplicate the value when both
operations agree rather than collapsing to a 1-entry
array on a composite import.

Use this when the API returns HTTP 200 for everything and
signals success / failure through a body field.  Pairs with
``successValues`` to define which values at this path mean
success.

Each entry is a DOT-PATH STRING.

successValues.description:
Per-operation list of values at ``successPath`` that mean
success.  TWO levels of array nesting:

- Outer array: one entry per ``requestType`` index.
  Length MUST match ``requestType`` length — duplicate
  the inner array when both operations agree rather than
  collapsing to a 1-entry outer array on a composite
  import.
- Inner array: the list of acceptable success values for
  that operation.

All comparisons are STRING comparisons regardless of the
actual response value type — the platform stringifies
numbers, booleans, etc. before comparing.

failPath.description:
Per-operation JSON path to a field that signals failure
even when HTTP returns 200.  Outer-array length MUST
match ``requestType`` length — duplicate when both
operations agree.  Same array semantics as ``successPath``.

Some APIs use only ``successPath`` (failure = absence of
success); others publish both an explicit success indicator
and an explicit failure indicator.  When both are
available, set both — the platform evaluates ``successPath``
first and falls through to ``failPath`` only when the
success check is inconclusive.

failValues.description:
Per-operation list of values at ``failPath`` that mean
failure.  Same two-level array shape and length contract
as ``successValues`` — outer length MUST match
``requestType`` length, duplicate the inner array on
composite imports when both operations agree.

Often used as the inverse of ``successValues`` (e.g.
``successValues: [["true"]]`` paired with
``failValues: [["false"]]``).

errorPath.description:
JSON path to the error message inside the response body.

**Note**: this field is NOT a per-operation array — it's a
single string applied to every operation.  Most APIs use
the same error-message field shape for both UPDATE and
CREATE responses, so the platform doesn't expose a per-op
override here.

allowArrayforSuccessPath.description: When true, allows array values at successPath during success evaluation.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Whether to evaluate ``successPath`` when its value is an array (rather than a single scalar).
When ``true``,
the success check passes if ANY element in the array matches ``successValues``.
Defaults to ``false`` (single-value comparison only).

hasHeader.description: When true, treats the first record in the response as a header row (for CSV responses).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
For CSV responses:
whether the first record is a header row that names the columns rather than carrying data.
Ignored for JSON / XML responses.

response.description:
Configuration for parsing and interpreting HTTP responses returned
from each write request the import issues.

**Critical: positional per-operation arrays**

Every field inside ``response`` (``resourcePath``, ``resourceIdPath``,
``successPath``, ``successValues``, ``failPath``, ``failValues``)
is an ARRAY whose outer length is positionally aligned with
``requestType`` / ``method`` / ``relativeURI``.  This is the
SAME positional-alignment contract as those three sibling
arrays — see ``relativeURI`` docs for the full explanation.

Each outer-array index describes how to parse the response from
the operation at that same index in ``requestType``:

- **Single-operation import** (``requestType: ["CREATE"]``):
  every response field is a 1-element array.
  ``successPath: ["ok"]`` means "for the one operation,
  look at path ``ok`` to detect success".
- **Composite upsert** (``requestType: ["UPDATE", "CREATE"]``):
  every response field is a 2-element array.  Index 0 parses
  the UPDATE response, index 1 parses the CREATE response.

**successValues / failValues — array of arrays**

``successValues`` and ``failValues`` carry an extra array level
because each operation can have MULTIPLE acceptable values:

- Outer array: one entry per operation (positional, as above).
- Inner array: the list of acceptable values for that operation.

Example:
```json
"requestType": ["UPDATE", "CREATE"],
"successPath": ["ok", "ok"],
"successValues": [["true", "1"], ["true"]]
```
Means: the UPDATE response is successful when ``ok`` is either
``"true"`` or ``"1"``; the CREATE response is successful only
when ``ok`` is ``"true"``.

**Always duplicate when operations agree (REQUIRED for composite)**

The outer-array length MUST match ``requestType`` length on
every response field.  When the UPDATE and CREATE responses
of the same connector look the same (which is the common
case — most APIs return the same shape from both endpoints),
DUPLICATE the entry so the array has the same length as
``requestType``.  Do NOT collapse to a 1-entry array on a
composite import.

```json
// ✅ Correct — explicit per-operation entries, even when identical
"requestType": ["UPDATE", "CREATE"],
"resourceIdPath": ["data.id", "data.id"],
"successPath": ["success", "success"],
"successValues": [["true"], ["true"]]
```

```json
// ❌ Wrong — 1-entry array on a composite import
"requestType": ["UPDATE", "CREATE"],
"resourceIdPath": ["data.id"],
"successPath": ["success"],
"successValues": [["true"]]
```

Why duplicate even when they agree:

- **UI parity.**  The Celigo UI renders one response-handling
  form per ``requestType`` index.  A 1-entry array on a
  composite import leaves the second operation's form panel
  empty, which looks like a half-built config to the user
  reviewing the saved import — even if it works at runtime.
- **Symmetric shape rule.**  ``relativeURI`` / ``method`` /
  ``requestType`` REQUIRE the entry count to match across
  all three (the runtime decider uses positional alignment).
  Making ``response.*`` follow the same "outer length ==
  requestType length" rule means there's ONE shape rule to
  remember, not two.
- **Unambiguous intent.**  A 2-entry duplicated array
  documents in the saved config that the developer
  considered both operations.  A 1-entry array could mean
  "both ops use this" or could mean "I forgot to fill in
  the second op."  Duplication eliminates the ambiguity.

When operations DIFFER (rare — different response shapes
per endpoint), set distinct values at each index.  Either
way the outer length always matches ``requestType``.

**Common llm mistake (DO not do THIS)**

Do NOT split a single dot-path into array segments thinking the
outer array represents path segments:

```json
// WRONG — the LLM expressed "data.id" as path segments
"requestType": ["UPDATE", "CREATE"],
"resourceIdPath": ["data", "id"]
```

This is interpreted by the platform as: UPDATE response's id is
at path ``data``, CREATE response's id is at path ``id`` — almost
never what the user wants.  The CORRECT shape is the single
dot-path expressed as ONE string per operation, duplicated to
match ``requestType`` length:

```json
"requestType": ["UPDATE", "CREATE"],
"resourceIdPath": ["data.id", "data.id"]
```

_asyncHelperId.description:
Reference to an AsyncHelper resource that polls an asynchronous
destination API on this import's behalf.

Set this ONLY when the destination API is genuinely asynchronous — it
acknowledges the submitted payload (HTTP 202, a job ticket) and ingests
it in the background, so completion must be polled for (e.g. bulk
image/file ingestion, large bulk-load endpoints). Most imports are
synchronous and need NO async helper; adding one to a synchronous
destination just adds polling overhead plus a status and result export
to maintain. When in doubt, leave it unset.

The referenced helper bundles the polling config plus a required status
export (polled to check progress) and a result export (fetches the
final payload). An import configured with an async helper cannot carry
its own transform, output filter, or preSavePage hook — put that
processing in the result export instead.

ignoreLookupName.description: Name of an entry in `lookups` used to check whether each record already exists, so `ignoreMissing`/`ignoreExisting` can skip it. Use it instead of `ignoreExtract` when existence must be resolved by a call to the target system rather than read from a field on the incoming record.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
## When NOT to set this field

Only valid for single-operation imports with either
``ignoreExisting: true`` or ``ignoreMissing: true`` set.
Composite (upsert) imports — those with both ``CREATE`` and
``UPDATE`` in ``requestType`` — use ``existingExtract`` /
``existingLookupName`` instead, because they route records
between two write paths rather than skipping them.

Name of a lookup defined in ``http.lookups`` that drives the SKIP-vs-PROCESS
decision when ``ignoreExisting`` or ``ignoreMissing`` is set.

The value MUST match the ``name`` of a lookup entry in ``http.lookups``.
This pattern adds **one HTTP request per record** at runtime — use
``ignoreExtract`` instead when the record already carries the field that signals
existence.

Pairs with either of the two skip-mode flags:

- With ``ignoreExisting: true`` (CREATE-only imports that should
  avoid duplicates): the named lookup probes the destination
  per record; if it returns a value, the record is treated as
  already-existing and is skipped; if it returns empty, the
  record is created.
- With ``ignoreMissing: true`` (UPDATE-only imports that should
  avoid creating new records): same probe — a non-empty result
  means the record exists and gets updated; empty means skip.

## Mutually exclusive with ``ignoreExtract``

Set EXACTLY ONE of ``ignoreExtract`` / ``ignoreLookupName`` when
``ignoreExisting`` or ``ignoreMissing`` is enabled.

lookups.description: Lookups referenced by `existingLookupName`/`ignoreLookupName` to resolve record existence against the destination system at runtime.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Lookup definitions executed over the HTTP connection.
Each entry issues an HTTP request (or reads from cache / static map) and
extracts a value that downstream layers reference by ``name``.

## How callers reference a lookup by name

Lookups are addressable by their ``name`` from three places:

- **Field mappings** — a mapping entry sets
  ``lookupName: "<name>"`` to resolve a field's value through
  the lookup.
- **Handlebars expressions** — anywhere handlebars is
  evaluated (relativeURI, headers, body), ``{{lookup "name"
  value}}`` calls the lookup with ``value`` as input.
- **Top-level decider fields** — ``http.existingLookupName`` /
  ``http.ignoreLookupName`` set to ``"<name>"`` make a lookup
  drive the import's UPDATE-vs-CREATE (composite upsert) or
  SKIP-vs-PROCESS (``ignoreExisting`` / ``ignoreMissing``)
  decision, respectively.  See those fields for the full
  decision semantics.

## Mirror invariant

The Celigo platform persists lookups in TWO locations on an HTTP
import: top-level ``lookups`` and ``http.lookups``.  Both arrays
MUST hold byte-for-byte identical content.  The import engine
and the MappingsAgent both maintain this mirror on every save —
callers never have to write both manually.

## Static vs dynamic vs cached

- **Static** — only ``map`` + optional ``default``.  No HTTP
  request issued.  Use for small controlled vocabularies.
- **Dynamic** — ``method`` + ``relativeURI`` (+ ``postBody``,
  ``headers``, ``extract``).  Issues a live HTTP request per
  lookup.  Adds one HTTP request per record at runtime — factor
  this into flow design for high-volume syncs.
- **Cached** — ``_lookupCacheId`` + ``extract``.  Reads from a
  pre-populated LookupCache resource.

name.description:
Unique identifier for this lookup. Mapping fields reference it
via ``lookupName`` and Handlebars expressions reference it via
``{{lookup.name}}``. Must be unique within this
resource's ``lookups`` array.

method.description:
HTTP method used to issue the lookup request. ``GET`` and
``POST`` are most common. Omit when using a static ``map`` or
``_lookupCacheId``.

relativeURI.description:
HTTP path (relative to the connection's base URL) that
resolves the lookup. Use Handlebars with triple braces to
inject values from the incoming record — e.g.
``/customers?email={{{email}}}`` or
``/accounts/{{{accountId}}}``.

postBody.description:
Request body template for POST / PUT / PATCH lookup methods.
Typically a JSON string with Handlebars placeholders —
``{"email":"{{{email}}}"}``. Ignored for GET / DELETE.

headers.description:
Optional custom headers to attach to the lookup request.
Useful for endpoints that need a different Accept header or
an auxiliary auth token separate from the connection-level
headers.

extract.description:
JSONPath expression that selects the lookup value from the
HTTP response body. ``$.`` prefix optional. Examples:
``$.data[0].id``, ``$.results.primaryKey``, ``id``.

_lookupCacheId.description:
Optional reference to a LookupCache resource. When set, the
lookup reads from the cache instead of issuing a live HTTP
request — useful for stable reference data that should be
pre-loaded.

map.description:
Optional static key→value object evaluated BEFORE the HTTP
request. When the incoming value matches a key, the mapped
value is returned without hitting the remote endpoint. Null
on dynamic lookups with no static map.

default.description:
Value returned when the HTTP request returns no usable
match. When omitted and ``allowFailures`` is false, an
unmatched lookup halts the record. Stored as null when no
fallback is configured.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Omit this field entirely when no fallback value is intended. The API rejects an empty string with [invalid_field] Invalid value '' for field 'default' — emitting default: "" to mean "no default" fails validation; leaving the key out is the valid spelling of that intent.
A fallback only takes effect on an allowed miss — pair a real default with allowFailures: true (or useDefaultOnMultipleMatches: true for the ambiguous-match case).

allowFailures.description:
When true, a lookup miss (no matching response and no
``default``) resolves to ``null`` and the import continues.
When false (default), a miss halts the record. May be
stored as null (treated as unset).

useDefaultOnMultipleMatches.description:
Controls behaviour when the response contains more than one
match. When true, the ``default`` value is returned instead
of raising an ambiguous-match error. When false (default),
multiple matches are treated as a failure.

ftp.description:
Defines where files are written on an FTP, FTPS, or SFTP server. Required when the
_connectionId field references an FTP/SFTP connection; must not be included for other
connection types. directoryPath selects the target folder and the file naming comes from
the import's file configuration.

_tpConnectorId.description:
Trading Partner Connector that supplies partner-specific B2B settings for this import.
When set, the import inherits the connector's pre-configured settings; omit to use only
the FTP connection details.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Identifier for the third-party connector utilized in the FTP integration,
serving as a unique and immutable reference that links the FTP configuration to
an external connector service.
This identifier is essential for accurately associating the FTP connection with
the intended third-party system,
enabling seamless and secure data transfer, synchronization,
and management through the specified connector.
It ensures that all FTP operations are correctly routed and managed via the external service,
supporting reliable integration workflows and maintaining system integrity
throughout the connection lifecycle.

## FIELD BEHAVIOR:
- Uniquely identifies the third-party connector associated with the FTP configuration.
- Acts as a key reference to bind FTP settings to a specific external connector service.
- Required when creating, updating, or managing FTP connections via third-party integrations.
- Typically immutable after initial assignment to preserve connection consistency.
- Used by system components to route FTP operations through the correct external connector.

## IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- Should be a string or numeric identifier that aligns with the third-party connector's identification scheme.
- Must be validated against the system's registry of available connectors to ensure validity.
- Should be set securely and protected from unauthorized modification.
- Updates to this identifier should be handled cautiously, with appropriate validation and impact assessment.
- Ensure the identifier complies with any formatting or naming conventions imposed by the third-party service.
- Transmit and store this identifier securely, using encryption where applicable.

## EXAMPLES:
- "connector_12345"
- "tpConnector-67890"
- "ftpThirdPartyConnector01"
- "extConnector_abcde"
- "thirdPartyFTP_001"

## IMPORTANT NOTES:
- This field is critical for correctly mapping FTP configurations to their corresponding third-party services.
- An incorrect or missing _tpConnectorId can lead to connection failures, data misrouting, or integration errors.
- Synchronization between this identifier and the third-party connector records must be maintained to avoid inconsistencies.
- Changes to this field may require re-authentication or reconfiguration of the FTP integration.
- Proper error handling should be implemented to manage cases where the identifier does not match any registered connector.

## DEPENDENCY CHAIN:
- Depends on the existence and registration of third-party connectors within the system.
- Referenced by FTP connection management modules, authentication services, and integration workflows.
- Interacts with authorization mechanisms to ensure secure access to third-party services.
- May influence logging, monitoring, and auditing processes related to FTP integrations.

directoryPath.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the FTP import form (fieldDefinitions/resources/imports/ftp.js: ftp.directoryPath is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
directoryPath.description:
Directory on the server where imported files are written, either absolute or relative to
the login directory; the FTP user must have write permission on it. Use forward slashes
regardless of server OS — paths are case-sensitive on UNIX/Linux servers. Supports
handlebars templates.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
The path to the directory on the FTP server where files will be accessed,
stored, or managed.
This path can be specified either as an absolute path starting from the root
directory of the FTP server or as a relative path based on the user's initial
directory upon login,
depending on the server's configuration and permissions.
It is essential that the path adheres to the FTP server's directory structure,
naming conventions,
and access controls to ensure successful file operations such as uploading,
downloading, listing, or deleting files.
The directoryPath serves as the primary reference point for all file-related
commands during an FTP session,
determining the scope and context of file management activities.

## FIELD BEHAVIOR:
- Defines the target directory location on the FTP server for all file-related operations.
- Supports both absolute and relative path formats, interpreted according to the FTP server's setup.
- Must comply with the server's directory hierarchy, naming rules, and access permissions.
- Used by the FTP client to navigate and perform operations within the specified directory.
- Influences the scope of accessible files and subdirectories during FTP sessions.
- Changes to this path affect subsequent file operations until updated or reset.

## IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- Validate the directory path format to ensure compatibility with the FTP server, typically using forward slashes (`/`) as separators.
- Normalize the path to remove redundant elements such as `.` (current directory) and `..` (parent directory) to prevent errors and security vulnerabilities.
- Handle scenarios where the specified directory does not exist by either creating it if permissions allow or returning a clear, descriptive error message.
- Properly encode special characters and escape sequences in the path to conform with FTP protocol requirements and server expectations.
- Provide informative and user-friendly error messages when the path is invalid, inaccessible, or lacks sufficient permissions.
- Sanitize input to prevent directory traversal attacks or unauthorized access to restricted areas.
- Consider server-specific behaviors such as case sensitivity, symbolic links, and virtual directories when interpreting the path.
- Ensure that path changes are atomic and consistent to avoid race conditions during concurrent FTP operations.

## EXAMPLES:
- `/uploads/images`
- `documents/reports/2024`
- `/home/user/data`
- `./backup`
- `../shared/resources`
- `/var/www/html`
- `projects/current`

## IMPORTANT NOTES:
- Access to the specified directory depends on the credentials used during FTP authentication.

fileName.description:
Name of the file written to the server, including its extension; do not include directory
separators — the location comes from directoryPath. Supports handlebars placeholders such
as items-{{timestamp}}.csv to generate a unique name per run.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When the user does not specify a file naming convention,
default to a timestamped filename such as "items-{{timestamp}}.csv" so each run
produces a unique file and avoids overwriting previous files.
Use a fixed filename only when the user explicitly requests overwriting or a fixed name.

The name of the file to be accessed, transferred,
or manipulated via FTP (File Transfer Protocol).
This property specifies the exact filename, including its extension,
uniquely identifying the file within the FTP directory.
It is critical for accurately targeting the file during operations such as upload,
download, rename, or delete.
The filename must be precise and comply with the naming conventions and
restrictions of the FTP server's underlying file system to avoid errors.
Case sensitivity depends on the server's operating system,
and special attention should be given to character encoding,
especially when handling non-ASCII or international characters.
The filename should not include any directory path separators,
as these are managed separately in directory or path properties.

## FIELD BEHAVIOR:
- Identifies the specific file within the FTP server directory for various file operations.
- Must include the file extension to ensure precise identification.
- Case sensitivity is determined by the FTP server's operating system.
- Excludes directory or path information; only the filename itself is specified.
- Used in conjunction with directory or path properties to locate the full file path.

## IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- Validate that the filename contains only characters allowed by the FTP server's file system.
- Ensure the filename is a non-empty, well-formed string without path separators.
- Normalize case if required to match server-specific case sensitivity rules.
- Properly handle encoding for special or international characters to prevent transfer errors.
- Combine with directory or path properties to construct the complete file location.
- Avoid embedding directory paths or separators within the filename property.

## EXAMPLES:
- "report.pdf"
- "image_2024.png"
- "backup_2023_12_31.zip"
- "data.csv"
- "items-{{timestamp}}.csv"

## IMPORTANT NOTES:
- The filename alone may not be sufficient to locate the file without the corresponding directory or path.
- Different FTP servers and operating systems may have varying rules regarding case sensitivity.
- Path separators such as "/" or "\" must not be included in the filename.
- Adherence to FTP server naming conventions and restrictions is essential to prevent errors.
- Be mindful of potential filename length limits imposed by the FTP server or protocol.

## DEPENDENCY CHAIN:
- Depends on FTP directory or path properties to specify the full file location.
- Utilized alongside FTP server credentials and connection settings.
- May be influenced by file transfer mode (binary or ASCII) based on the file type.

inProgressFileName.x-celigo-ui-override: The FTP import form requires this once its "Use temp file" toggle is on (fieldDefinitions/resources/imports/ftp.js: 'ftp.inProgressFileName' requiredWhen ftp.useTempFile is true; blob mode 'ftp.blobInProgressFileName' requiredWhen ftp.blobUseTempFile is true). The toggles are form-only and are not saved — the form derives them from whether this field is set — so the API has no field to condition on and saves the import with or without the name.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The form's requiredWhen depends on a toggle that is never persisted, so no API-side condition exists; the server saves an FTP import with or without the name.

inProgressFileName.description:
Temporary name the file carries while its upload is in progress, preventing other systems
from processing a partially transferred file; it is renamed to its final name once the
upload completes. Its presence is what the UI shows as "Use temp file while upload in
progress": set it to turn the temporary name on, omit it to turn it off. Include a
handlebars uniqueness token (e.g. {{timestamp}}) when one file is written per flow run.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
inProgressFileName is the designated temporary filename assigned to a file
during the FTP upload process to clearly indicate that the file transfer is
currently underway and not yet complete.
This naming convention serves as a safeguard to prevent other systems or
processes from prematurely accessing,
processing, or locking the file before the upload finishes successfully.
Typically, once the upload is finalized,
the file is renamed to its intended permanent filename,
signaling that it is ready for further use or processing.
Utilizing an in-progress filename helps maintain data integrity,
avoid conflicts,
and streamline workflow automation in environments where files are continuously
transferred and monitored.
It plays a critical role in managing file state visibility,
ensuring that incomplete or partially transferred files are not mistakenly processed,
which could lead to data corruption or inconsistent system behavior.

## FIELD BEHAVIOR:
- Acts as a temporary marker for files actively being uploaded via FTP or similar protocols.
- Prevents other processes, systems, or automated workflows from accessing or processing the file until the upload is fully complete.
- The file is renamed atomically from the inProgressFileName to the final intended filename upon successful upload completion.
- Helps manage concurrency, avoid file corruption, partial reads, or race conditions during file transfer.
- Indicates the current state of the file within the transfer lifecycle, providing clear visibility into upload progress.
- Supports cleanup mechanisms by identifying orphaned or stale temporary files resulting from interrupted uploads.

## IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- Choose a unique, consistent, and easily identifiable naming pattern distinct from final filenames to clearly denote the in-progress status.
- Commonly use suffixes or prefixes such as ".inprogress", ".tmp", "_uploading", or similar conventions that are recognized across systems.
- Ensure the FTP server and client support atomic renaming operations to avoid partial file visibility or race conditions.
- Verify that the chosen temporary filename does not collide with existing files in the target directory to prevent overwriting or confusion.
- Maintain consistent naming conventions across all related systems, scripts, and automation tools for clarity and maintainability.
- Implement robust cleanup routines to detect and remove orphaned or stale in-progress files from failed or abandoned uploads.
- Coordinate synchronization between upload completion and renaming to prevent premature processing or file locking issues.

## EXAMPLES:
- "datafile.csv.inprogress"
- "upload.tmp"
- "report_20240615.tmp"
- "file_upload_inprogress"
- "transaction_12345.uploading"

backupDirectoryPath.description:
Directory on the same server where a copy of each written file is retained after a
successful import; if omitted, no server-side backup is kept. Supports static paths or
handlebars templates.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
backupDirectoryPath specifies the file system path to the directory where backup
files are stored during FTP operations.
This directory serves as the designated location for saving copies of files
before they are overwritten or deleted,
ensuring that original data can be recovered if necessary.
The path can be either absolute or relative, depending on the system context,
and must conform to the operating system's file path conventions.
It is essential that this path is valid, accessible,
and writable by the FTP service or application performing the backups to
guarantee reliable backup creation and data integrity.
Proper configuration of this path is critical to prevent data loss and to
maintain a secure and organized backup environment.

## FIELD BEHAVIOR:
- Specifies the target directory for storing backup copies of files involved in FTP transactions.
- Activated only when backup functionality is enabled within the FTP process.
- Requires the path to be valid, accessible, and writable to ensure successful backup creation.
- Supports both absolute and relative paths, with relative paths resolved against a defined base directory.
- If unset or empty, backup operations may be disabled or fallback to a default directory if configured.

## IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- Validate the existence of the directory and verify write permissions before initiating backups.
- Normalize paths to handle trailing slashes, redundant separators, and platform-specific path formats.
- Provide clear and actionable error messages if the directory is invalid, inaccessible, or lacks necessary permissions.
- Support environment variables or placeholders for dynamic path resolution where applicable.
- Enforce security best practices by restricting access to the backup directory to authorized users or processes only.
- Ensure sufficient disk space is available in the backup directory to accommodate backup files without interruption.
- Implement concurrency controls such as file locking or synchronization if multiple backup operations may occur simultaneously.

## EXAMPLES:
- "/var/ftp/backups"
- "C:\\ftp\\backup"
- "./backup_files"
- "/home/user/ftp_backup"

## IMPORTANT NOTES:
- The backup directory must have adequate storage capacity to prevent backup failures due to insufficient space.
- Permissions must allow the FTP process or service to create and modify files within the directory.
- Backup files may contain sensitive or confidential data; appropriate security measures should be enforced to protect them.
- Path formatting should align with the conventions of the underlying operating system to avoid errors.

jdbc.description:
Configuration for JDBC import operations. Defines how data is written to a database
via a JDBC connection.

**Query type determines which fields are required**

| queryType        | Required fields              | Do NOT set        |
|------------------|------------------------------|-------------------|
| ["per_record"]   | query (array of SQL strings) | bulkInsert        |
| ["per_page"]     | query (array of SQL strings) | bulkInsert        |
| ["bulk_insert"]  | bulkInsert object            | query             |
| ["bulk_load"]    | bulkLoad object              | query             |

**Critical:** query IS AN ARRAY OF STRINGS
The query field must be an array of plain strings, NOT a single string and NOT an array of objects.
Correct: ["INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('{{{name}}}')"]
Wrong: "INSERT INTO users ..."
Wrong: [{"query": "INSERT INTO users ..."}]

query.description:
Array of SQL query strings to execute. REQUIRED when queryType is ["per_record"] or ["per_page"].

Each element is a complete SQL statement as a plain string. Typically contains a single query.

Use Handlebars {{fieldName}} syntax to inject values from incoming records.

**Format — array of strings**
- CORRECT: ["INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('{{{name}}}', '{{{email}}}')"]
- WRONG: "INSERT INTO users ..."  (not an array)
- WRONG: [{"query": "INSERT INTO users ..."}]  (objects are invalid — causes Cast error)

**Examples**
- INSERT: ["INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('{{{name}}}', '{{{email}}}')"]
- UPDATE: ["UPDATE inventory SET qty = {{{quantity}}} WHERE sku = '{{{sku}}}'"]
- MERGE/UPSERT: ["MERGE INTO target USING (SELECT CAST(? AS VARCHAR) AS email) AS src ON target.email = src.email WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET name = ? WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)"]

**String vs numeric values in handlebars**
- Use triple braces so the raw value is emitted; double braces emit the value already single-quoted, so wrapping them in quotes double-quotes it.
- Strings: supply the quotes yourself — '{{{name}}}'
- Numbers: no quotes — {{{quantity}}}

x-enumDescriptions.bulk_insert: Batch INSERT via multi-row VALUES clause for efficient bulk data loading.
x-enumDescriptions.per_record: Execute one SQL statement per record, giving full control over individual record SQL.
x-enumDescriptions.per_page: Execute one SQL statement per page (batch) of records.
x-enumDescriptions.bulk_load: Stage data as a file and load via database-native COPY/bulk mechanism for maximum throughput.

queryType.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the JDBC import form (jdbc.queryType is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
queryType.description:
Execution strategy for the SQL operation. REQUIRED. Must be an array with one value.

**Decision tree**

1. If UPDATE or UPSERT/MERGE → ["per_record"] (set query field)
2. If INSERT with "ignore existing" / "skip duplicates" / match logic → ["per_record"] (set query field)
3. If pure INSERT with no duplicate checking → ["bulk_insert"] (set bulkInsert object)
4. If high-volume bulk load → ["bulk_load"] (set bulkLoad object)

**Critical relationship to other fields**
| queryType        | REQUIRES              | DO NOT SET   |
|------------------|-----------------------|--------------|
| ["per_record"]   | query (array)         | bulkInsert   |
| ["per_page"]     | query (array)         | bulkInsert   |
| ["bulk_insert"]  | bulkInsert object     | query        |
| ["bulk_load"]    | bulkLoad object       | query        |

**Examples**
- Per-record upsert: ["per_record"]
- Bulk insert: ["bulk_insert"]
- Bulk load: ["bulk_load"]

bulkInsert.description:
Bulk insert configuration. REQUIRED when queryType is ["bulk_insert"]. DO NOT SET when queryType is ["per_record"].

Enables efficient batch insertion of records into a database table without per-record SQL.

tableName.description:
Target database table name for bulk insert. REQUIRED.
Can include schema qualifiers (e.g., "schema.tableName").

batchSize.description:
Number of records per batch during bulk insert.
Larger values improve throughput but use more memory.
Common values: "1000", "5000".

bulkLoad.description: Bulk load configuration. REQUIRED when queryType is ["bulk_load"]. Uses database-native bulk loading for maximum throughput.

tableName.description:
Target database table name for bulk load. REQUIRED.
Can include schema qualifiers (e.g., "schema.tableName").

primaryKeys.description:
Primary key column names for upsert/merge during bulk load.
When set, existing rows matching these keys are updated; non-matching rows are inserted.
Example: ["id"] or ["order_id", "product_id"] for composite keys.

overrideMergeOrInsertQuery.description:
When true, a custom merge/insert query replaces the auto-generated statement for the
bulk load, enabling ignore-existing logic or conditional updates.

name.description:
Unique identifier for this lookup. Mapping fields reference it
via `lookupName` and Handlebars expressions reference it via
`{{lookup "name" value}}`. Must be unique within this
resource's `lookups` array.

query.description: SQL query for the lookup (e.g., "SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = '{{{email}}}'").
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
SQL `SELECT` statement that resolves the lookup value.
Inject values from the incoming record with Handlebars — JDBC queries use triple braces:
`SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = '{{{email}}}'`.
Returns a single row;
use `extract` to pick a column when multiple are selected.
examples: SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = '{{{email}}}'

extract.description:
JSONPath-style expression that selects the value from the
query result row (e.g. `id`, `details.price`). Omit when
the query returns a single scalar.

_lookupCacheId.description:
Optional reference to a LookupCache resource. When set, the
lookup reads from the cache instead of issuing a live SQL
query — useful for stable reference data that should be
pre-loaded.

allowFailures.description:
When true, a lookup miss (no matching row and no `default`)
resolves to `null` and the import continues. When false
(default), a miss halts the record.

map.description:
Optional static key→value object evaluated BEFORE the SQL
query. When the incoming value matches a key, the mapped
value is returned without querying the database.

default.description:
Value returned when the query matches no rows. When omitted
and `allowFailures` is false, an unmatched lookup halts the
record.

lookups.description:
Lookup definitions executed against the JDBC connection. Each entry
runs a `SELECT` and extracts a value used by field mappings
(referenced via `lookupName`) or Handlebars expressions
(referenced via `{{lookup "name" value}}`).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
## Mirror invariant
The Celigo platform persists lookups in TWO locations on a JDBC
import: top-level `lookups` and `jdbc.lookups`. Both arrays
must hold byte-for-byte identical content — the MappingsAgent
writes both on every save.

mongodb.description: Configuration for MongoDB imports. Contains only the MongoDB-specific properties; import-level fields such as ignoreExisting, ignoreMissing, name, and description are set on the parent import, not here.

x-enumDescriptions.insertMany: Insert multiple documents into the MongoDB collection in a single batch operation.
x-enumDescriptions.updateOne: Update a single existing document in the MongoDB collection that matches the filter criteria.

method.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the MongoDB import form (mongodb.method is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
method.description: Write operation performed against the MongoDB collection for each record.

collection.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the MongoDB import form (mongodb.collection is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
collection.description:
MongoDB collection that receives the imported records.
Collection names are case-sensitive and must not start with the reserved "system." prefix.

filter.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the MongoDB import form when method is updateOne (mongodb.filter is required:true, visibleWhen method=updateOne).
filter.description:
MongoDB query filter that selects the document each updateOne applies to; required when
method is updateOne. Supports standard MongoDB query operators and dot notation, and
handlebars placeholders to reference the incoming record's fields.

document.description: Content of the document written to the collection (used when method is insertMany), as a JSON string that can include nested documents and arrays and handlebars placeholders.

update.description:
Modifications applied to matching documents (used when method is updateOne), using MongoDB update operators such as $set, $inc, or $push.
A complete document without operators replaces the matched document entirely.

upsert.description:
When true, inserts a new document built from the update criteria if no existing document matches the filter.
When false, records with no matching document are skipped and nothing is inserted.

ignoreExtract.description:
Path to the field in the source record that identifies existing records. When that field has a value, the record is treated as existing and skipped.
Only used when the import-level ignoreExisting flag is true; do not set it otherwise.
Enclose field names containing special characters in square brackets (for example, [vendor-code]), and reference array items with an index, such as items[0].id.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Set this together with the import-level ignoreExisting flag; both must be set for skip-existing behavior to work, and ignoreExisting is not part of this mongodb object.

Use the field path from the incoming source data, not the target MongoDB field. When the prompt names an identifier field (for example, "ignore existing customers indicated by the id field"), use that field.

ignoreLookupFilter.description:
JSON-stringified MongoDB query filter used to find existing documents in the target collection when the import-level ignoreExisting flag is true.
If the query matches a document, the incoming record is treated as existing and skipped.
Use Handlebars placeholders to reference values from the incoming record, for example "{\"email\":\"{{email}}\"}".
Unlike ignoreExtract, which only checks whether a field on the incoming record has a value, this filter queries the MongoDB collection itself.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: The value must be a JSON string (stringify the filter object); filter keys must match field names in the MongoDB collection, and Handlebars variables must match fields in the incoming data.

netsuite.description: Configuration for NetSuite imports (legacy adaptor; use netsuite_da / NetSuiteDistributedImport for SuiteApp 2.0).

x-celigo-canon.reason: Inner requireds are stub-gated — the server writes bookkeeping netsuite stubs (bare preferences or lookups) onto imports of other adaptorTypes, so operation and recordType are required only when user-config keys are present.

name.description: Unique name for this lookup, referenced from mappings and handlebars templates with `{{lookup 'name' value}}`.

recordType.description: NetSuite record type searched by a dynamic lookup (for example, `customer`, `salesOrder`). Set with `searchField` or `expression`; omit for a static `map` lookup.

searchField.description: NetSuite field the dynamic lookup searches on (for example, `externalid`). Must be a searchable field on `recordType`. Use this or `expression`.

expression.description: NetSuite search expression evaluated at runtime to select matching records (for example, `["recipient","is","123"]`). Use this or `searchField`.

resultField.description:
Field on the matched NetSuite record whose value the lookup returns (for example, `internalid`).
Supports dot notation for nested fields.

map.description: Static lookup table with input values as keys and their corresponding output values. Use instead of a NetSuite search for fixed value translations. The platform stores `null` here on search-driven lookups.

default.description: Fallback value returned when the lookup finds no match. Used together with `allowFailures`. Stored as `null` when not configured.

allowFailures.description: When true, an unmatched lookup falls back to `default` and processing continues; when false, an unmatched lookup fails the record.

_id.description: Server-assigned unique identifier for this lookup entry.

lookups.description: Lookup definitions used to resolve reference values during the import, using either a static `map` or a dynamic NetSuite record search.

x-enumDescriptions.add: Create a new record in NetSuite.
x-enumDescriptions.update: Update an existing record in NetSuite, identified via internalIdLookup.
x-enumDescriptions.addupdate: Upsert — update the record if found, otherwise create a new one.
x-enumDescriptions.attach: Attach one NetSuite record to another record.
x-enumDescriptions.detach: Detach a previously attached NetSuite record from another record.
x-enumDescriptions.delete: Delete an existing record from NetSuite, identified via internalIdLookup.

operation.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the NetSuite import form (operation is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
operation.description:
Operation to perform on NetSuite records, as a plain string (the API lowercases the value).
For `update`, `addupdate`, and `delete`, also set internalIdLookup so existing records can be found; for `add` with ignoreExisting, set internalIdLookup to check for duplicates before creating.
Default to `addupdate` when the intent is "sync", "upsert", or "create or update"; use `add` for plain "create" or "insert".
Do not wrap the value in an object like `{"type": "addupdate"}` — that fails validation.

isFileProvider.description:
When true, enables file operations against NetSuite — browsing, uploading, downloading, updating, and deleting files.
When false or omitted, file-related operations are unavailable through this import.

customFieldMetadata.description: Metadata describing the custom fields defined on the target NetSuite record type, used to validate and process custom field data during the import.

recordType.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the NetSuite import form (recordType is required:true) for record imports. File-provider imports (isFileProvider true) are built by the file-provider form, which sets `file` instead of recordType — the schema's if/then/else mirrors that split.
recordType.description:
NetSuite record type this import writes to (e.g. customer, salesOrder, invoice).
Use the exact NetSuite internal record type identifier; both standard and custom record types are supported.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Do not require recordType when isFileProvider is true — file-provider configs are a current server-accepted shape carrying operation and file but no recordType.

recordTypeId.description: The unique identifier specifying the record type within NetSuite. Determines the applicable schema, fields, validation rules, and processing logic. Use exact NetSuite record type identifiers such as standard types or custom record IDs.

retryUpdateAsAdd.description:
When true, an update that fails because the target record does not exist is automatically retried as an add.
When false or unset, update failures error immediately without retrying.
May create duplicate records if the update failed for a reason other than a missing record.

batchSize.description:
Number of records sent to NetSuite per API call.
Larger batches reduce the number of calls but increase memory use and timeout risk per call.

extract.description: Path used to extract the value for the internal ID lookup.

searchField.description: The NetSuite record field used as the key attribute for the internal ID lookup search. Should be a unique or indexed field to ensure accurate matches. Must correspond to a valid, searchable field on the target record type.

expression.description:
NetSuite search expression that filters which records match the lookup.
Supports logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), comparison operators, and nested conditions, evaluated at runtime against current data.

internalIdLookup.description:
Configuration for locating existing NetSuite records by internal ID.
Required when operation is `update`, `addupdate`, or `delete`; also used with `add` plus ignoreExisting to check for duplicates.

ignoreReadOnlyFields.description: When true, silently skips read-only fields during update operations instead of raising errors.

warningAsError.description: When true, treats NetSuite warnings as errors, causing the operation to fail immediately.

skipCustomMetadataRequests.description: When true, skips custom metadata requests during NetSuite API operations to improve performance.

preferences.description: Preferences that control how NetSuite handles the import operation.

name.description:
Filename for the file in the NetSuite File Cabinet, without any folder or path information.
Must be unique within its folder; include the file extension (e.g. .pdf, .csv).

fileType.description:
NetSuite file type that governs how the file is processed, stored, and displayed.
Must match the actual content format of the file.

folder.description:
Folder in the NetSuite File Cabinet where the file is stored, as a numeric folder ID or a folder path.
Updating this on an existing file moves the file to the specified folder.

folderInternalId.description:
Internal ID of the File Cabinet folder where the file is stored.
Must reference an existing folder; changing it moves the file to a different folder.

internalId.description:
NetSuite internal ID of an existing file, used to target it for retrieval, updates, or deletion.
Assigned by NetSuite when the file is created and cannot be changed.

backupFolderInternalId.description: Internal ID of the File Cabinet folder where backup files are stored.

file.description: Configuration for the file to upload to or update in the NetSuite File Cabinet.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Inner requireds are stub-gated — the server writes bookkeeping netsuite_da stubs (empty lookups/mapping, or missingOrCorruptedDAConfig) onto imports of other adaptorTypes, so operation and recordType are required only when user-config keys are present.

netsuite_da.description:
Configuration for NetSuite Distributed (SuiteApp 2.0) import operations — the primary sub-schema for the NetSuiteDistributedImport adaptorType. The API field name is "netsuite_da".
operation and recordType are required. The server may attach empty bookkeeping stubs of
this object (empty lookups/mapping, or missingOrCorruptedDAConfig) to imports of other
adaptor types; stubs omit these fields. Set internalIdLookup so existing records
can be found when operation is update, addupdate, or delete.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
## KEY FIELDS
- operation: REQUIRED — the NetSuite operation (add, update, addupdate, etc.)
- recordType: REQUIRED — the NetSuite record type (e.g., "customer", "salesorder")
- mapping: field mappings from source data to NetSuite fields
- internalIdLookup: how to find existing records for update/addupdate/delete
- restletVersion: defaults to "suiteapp2.0"; fixed once the step is created (recreate/clone to change)

x-enumDescriptions.add: Create a new record in NetSuite.
x-enumDescriptions.update: Update an existing record in NetSuite, requires internalIdLookup.
x-enumDescriptions.addupdate: Upsert — update the record if found, otherwise create a new one.
x-enumDescriptions.attach: Attach one NetSuite record to another record.
x-enumDescriptions.detach: Detach a previously attached NetSuite record from another record.
x-enumDescriptions.delete: Delete an existing record from NetSuite, requires internalIdLookup.

operation.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the NetSuite import form (operation is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
operation.description:
Operation to perform on the target NetSuite record, as a plain string. Required.
For `update`, `addupdate`, and `delete`, also set internalIdLookup so existing records can be found.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
## GUIDANCE
- Default to "addupdate" when user says "sync", "upsert", or "create or update".
- Use "add" when user says "create" or "insert" without mentioning updates.
- For "update", "addupdate", and "delete", you MUST also set internalIdLookup.

## IMPORTANT
This field is a string, NOT an object. Set it directly: "operation": "addupdate"
Do NOT send {"type": "addupdate"} — that causes a Cast error.

recordType.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the NetSuite import form (recordType is required:true). Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.
recordType.description:
NetSuite record type to import into (e.g. "customer", "salesorder", "customrecord_myrecord" for custom record types). Required.
Must match a valid NetSuite record type identifier.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Use the NetSuite internal record-type id: lowercase, no spaces,
no camelCase (e.g.
`salesorder` — NOT `salesOrder` — and `itemfulfillment` — NOT `itemFulfillment`).
Custom records use `customrecord_<id>`.

Common standard record types in active integrations (ordered most → least frequent):
`salesorder`, `customer`, `invoice`, `itemfulfillment`,
`customerrefund`, `returnauthorization`, `creditmemo`, `inventoryitem`,
`customerpayment`, `customerdeposit`, `journalentry`, `itemreceipt`,
`cashrefund`, `cashsale`, `purchaseorder`, `deposit`, `contact`,
`transferorder`, `inventoryadjustment`, `vendorbill`, `vendor`, `job`,
`noninventoryitem`, `employee`.

recordIdentifier.description:
Custom record identifier, used to identify the specific record type when
importing into custom record types.

x-enumDescriptions.suitebundle: Legacy SuiteBundle RESTlet version; slated for deprecation — NetSuite no longer updates SuiteScript 1.0.
x-enumDescriptions.suiteapp2.0: SuiteApp 2.0 RESTlet version using SuiteScript 2.0, the modern default.

restletVersion.description:
Version of the NetSuite RESTlet to use, as a plain string.
Defaults to "suiteapp2.0" when useSS2Restlets is true, "suitebundle" otherwise; rarely needs to be set explicitly for modern integrations.
The version is fixed when the step is created — the Advanced selector is disabled on existing steps, and migrating an existing step to a different version means recreating or cloning it.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Do not wrap the value in an object like `{"type": "suiteapp2.0"}` — that causes a Cast error.

The NetSuite API version cannot be changed on an existing step — the UI
disables the selector once the step is saved. When asked to migrate an
existing step off the SuiteBundle (or between versions), do not update
this field in place; the migration path is recreating or cloning the
step with the new version.

SuiteScript hooks are a separate setting from the step's API version:
hook code must be written for the same SuiteScript version as the step
(1.0 and 2.x are not interchangeable), and migrating a hook is its own
task — flag it whenever migrating a step that carries hooks.

Author new steps with suiteapp2.0 unless the user explicitly requires a
legacy version — NetSuite no longer updates SuiteScript 1.0 and Celigo
plans to deprecate the SuiteBundle option.

useSS2Restlets.description:
When true, uses SuiteScript 2.0 RESTlets and restletVersion defaults to "suiteapp2.0".
Defaults to true for modern integrations.
Set at step creation together with restletVersion — the same creation-time-only constraint applies (see restletVersion).

missingOrCorruptedDAConfig.description:
When true, the Distributed Adaptor configuration is missing or corrupted.
Set by the system — do not set manually.

batchSize.description:
Number of records to process per batch. Controls how many records are sent
to NetSuite in a single API call. Typical values: 50-200.

internalIdLookup.description:
Configuration for looking up existing NetSuite records to match against incoming data.
Required when operation is "update", "addupdate", or "delete".
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Two ways to specify the lookup, picked per import:

- **Simple form** — set `searchField` + `operator` (+ optional
  `extract`).  Use for single-criterion lookups against a built-in
  NetSuite field.  The platform builds the equivalent search
  expression for you at runtime.
- **Expression form** — set `expression` to a NetSuite search-
  expression literal.  Use for compound (AND/OR) lookups, custom-
  record-field lookups (`custbody_*` / `custrecord_*` /
  `custentity_*`), and the `anyof` operator that the simple form
  doesn't cover.  When `expression` is set, `searchField` /
  `operator` / `extract` are ignored.

Production usage:
`expression` is set on ~99.6% of active `internalIdLookup` blocks (55K imports),
so the expression form is the dominant pattern in the field.

extract.description: Path in the source record to extract the lookup value from (e.g. "internalId" or "externalId").
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Path on the incoming source record (NOT the post-mapped record) whose value drives the lookup.
Used with the simple form (`searchField` + `operator`).
Common values: `"internalId"`, `"externalId"`, `"id"`.
Ignored when `expression` is set.

NetSuite field the simple-form lookup queries against.
Common values: `"externalId"`, `"internalId"`, `"email"`, `"tranId"`,
`"name"`.
Ignored when `expression` is set.

Comparison operator for the simple-form lookup.
Common values: `"is"` (exact match),
`"anyof"` (matches any of the given internal-id values), `"contains"`,
`"startswith"`, `"equalto"`.
Ignored when `expression` is set.

expression.description: NetSuite search expression for complex lookup conditions, used for multi-field or conditional lookups.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
NetSuite search-expression literal as a JSON string.
The expression is evaluated at runtime — Handlebars renders `{{...}}`
substitutions FIRST against the incoming source record (pre-mapped),
then the substituted expression is sent to NetSuite as a saved-search query.

## Handlebars conventions (production grounded)

- **No `record.` prefix** — substitutions reference top-level
  source-record fields directly.  `{{{id}}}` / `{{{Id}}}` /
  `{{{externalid}}}` / `{{{[Internal ID]}}}` — NOT
  `{{{record.id}}}`.  Production: only 122 / 55,328 expressions
  (0.2%) use the `record.` prefix; the dominant convention is
  top-level paths.
- **Triple braces `{{{...}}}`** are the preferred form (78% of
  production); double-brace `{{...}}` also works for cases
  where you want the platform's default HTML-escape (rare in
  this field).
- **Bracket notation for field names with spaces or special
  chars**: `{{{[Field With Spaces]}}}`, `{{{[Internal ID]}}}`.
  Anchored to ~10% of production expressions.

## Canonical patterns

### Simple lookup by internal ID (most common — 8.4% of all expressions)

`["internalid","is","{{{id}}}"]`

Use when the source record carries the destination NetSuite
internal-id directly (e.g., from a prior lookup, response
mapping, or cross-reference field).

### Multi-match by internal ID

`["internalid","anyof","{{{id}}}"]`

Same as above but uses `anyof` to match an internal-id from a
comma-separated list value.  `anyof` is only available via the
expression form (the simple `operator` field doesn't carry it).

### Lookup by external ID

`["externalid","is","{{{Id}}}"]` /
`["externalid","is","{{{id}}}"]`

Use when the source record's primary key is stored in NetSuite as
an `externalid` (cross-reference scenarios — Shopify, SFCC,
Amazon, etc., where the platform-specific id is the externalid).

### Lookup by custom-record field

`["custbody_celigo_etail_order_id","is","{{{id}}}"]`
`["custentity_celigo_sfio_sf_id","is","{{{Id}}}"]`
`["custrecord_celigo_shopify_payout_id","is","{{{id}}}"]`

Use when the destination NetSuite record carries a custom field
holding the source-system id.  The `cust*_*` field id MUST
match the script-id of an existing custom field on the target
record type (e.g., `custbody_*` on transactions,
`custentity_*` on entities, `custrecord_*` on custom records
and lists).

### Compound AND lookup (multiple criteria)

`[["custbody_celigo_amzio_settlement_id","is","{{{[Settlement Id]}}}"],"AND",["custbody_celigo_amzio_accounts","is","{{{[Amazon Account Internal Id]}}}"]]`

Use when the destination record needs more than one field to
uniquely identify it (composite-key scenarios — Amazon
settlements, multi-store integrations).  Each criterion is a
`[field, operator, value]` triple; the outer array alternates
triples and operators (`"AND"` / `"OR"`).

### Compound with OR / nested grouping

`[["custbody_celigo_etail_order_id","is","{{{order_id}}}"],"AND",["custbody_celigo_etail_order_fulfilled","is","T"],"AND",[["custbody_celigo_etail_fulfillment_id","is","{{{id}}}"],"OR",["custbody_celigo_etail_fulfillment_id","isempty",""]]]`

`OR` works the same as `AND`; nesting groups via inner
arrays.  Use `"isempty"` (with empty-string value) to match
unset fields.

## Anti-patterns

- DO NOT prefix substitutions with `record.` — top-level paths
  are the convention.
- DO NOT use `jsonSerialize` here — search expressions take
  scalar literals, not serialized JSON.  Use `{{{id}}}` or
  `{{{[Field Name]}}}` directly.

hooks.description:
Script hooks for custom processing at different stages of the import.
Each hook references a SuiteScript file and function.

preMap.description: Runs before field mapping is applied.

fileInternalId.description: NetSuite internal ID of the SuiteScript file. Null on hook stubs where no SuiteScript file has been selected.

function.description: Name of the function to execute.

configuration.description: Configuration object passed to the hook function. Null when the hook carries no static parameters.

postMap.description: Runs after field mapping, before submission to NetSuite.

fileInternalId.description: NetSuite internal ID of the SuiteScript file. Null on hook stubs where no SuiteScript file has been selected.

function.description: Name of the function to execute.

configuration.description: Configuration object passed to the hook function. Null when the hook carries no static parameters.

postSubmit.description: Runs after the record is submitted to NetSuite.

fileInternalId.description: NetSuite internal ID of the SuiteScript file. Null on hook stubs where no SuiteScript file has been selected.

function.description: Name of the function to execute.

configuration.description: Configuration object passed to the hook function. Null when the hook carries no static parameters.

mapping.description:
NetSuite-specific Mapper 1.0 field mappings (the "DA" dialect).
Used by `NetSuiteDistributedImport` exclusively — NetSuite's
Distributed Adaptor cannot consume generic v1 mappings or the
Mapper 2.0 shape because it needs sublist, subrecord, and
conditional lookup semantics the generic schemas don't model.

Field-level shape: `fields` for body columns, `lists` for

lookups.description:
Configuration for value-to-value transformations using lookup tables.

**Purpose**

Lookups provide a way to translate values from one system to another. They transform
input values into output values using either static mapping tables or
dynamic lookup caches.

**Lookup mechanisms**

There are two distinct lookup mechanisms available:

1. **Static Lookups**: Define a simple key-value map object and store it as part of your resource
   - Best for: Small, fixed sets of values that rarely change
   - Implementation: Configure the `map` object with input-to-output value mappings
   - Example: Country codes, status values, simple translations

2. **Dynamic Lookups**: Reference an existing 'Lookup Cache' resource in your Celigo account
   - Best for: Large datasets, frequently changing values, or complex reference data
   - Implementation: Configure `_lookupCacheId` to reference cached data maintained independently
   - Example: Product catalogs, customer databases, pricing information

**Property usage**

There are two mutually exclusive ways to configure lookups, depending on which mechanism you choose:

1. **For Static Mappings**: Configure the `map` property with a direct key-value object
   ```json
   "map": {"US": "United States", "CA": "Canada"}
   ```

2. **For Dynamic Lookups**: Configure the following properties:
   - `_lookupCacheId`: Reference to the lookup cache resource
   - `extract`: JSON path to extract specific value from the returned lookup object

**When to use**

Lookups are ideal for:

1. **Value Translation**: Mapping codes or IDs to human-readable values

2. **Data Enrichment**: Adding related information to records during processing

3. **Normalization**: Ensuring consistent formatting of values across systems

**Implementation details**

Lookups can be referenced in:

1. **Field Mappings**: Direct use in field transformation configurations

2. **Handlebars Templates**: Use within templates with the syntax:
   ```
   {{lookup 'lookupName' record.fieldName}}
   ```

**Example usage**

```json
"lookups": [
  {
    "name": "countryCodeToName",
    "map": {
      "US": "United States",
      "CA": "Canada",
      "UK": "United Kingdom"
    },
    "default": "Unknown Country",
    "allowFailures": true
  },
  {
    "name": "productDetails",
    "_lookupCacheId": "60a2c4e6f321d800129a1a3c",
    "extract": "$.details.price",
    "allowFailures": false
  }
]
```

name.description:
Unique identifier for the lookup table within this configuration.

This name must be unique within the scope where the lookup is defined and is used to reference
the lookup in handlebars templates with the syntax {{lookup 'name' value}}.

Choose descriptive names that indicate the transformation purpose, such as:
- "countryCodeToName" for country code to full name conversion
- "statusMapping" for status code translations
- "departmentCodes" for department code to name mapping

map.description:
The lookup mapping table as key-value pairs. The platform stores `null`
here on dynamic lookups, which resolve values at runtime instead of
from a static table.

This object contains the input values as keys and their corresponding
output values. When a input value matches a key in this object,
it will be replaced with the corresponding value.

The map should be kept to a reasonable size (typically under 100 entries)
for optimal performance. For larger mapping requirements, consider using
dynamic lookups instead.

Maps can include:
- Simple code to name conversions: {"US": "United States"}
- Status transformations: {"A": "Active", "I": "Inactive"}
- ID to name mappings: {"100": "Marketing", "200": "Sales"}

Values can be strings, numbers, or booleans, but all are stored as strings
in the configuration.

_lookupCacheId.description:
Reference to a LookupCache resource that contains the reference data for the lookup.

**Purpose**

This field connects the lookup to an external data source that has been cached in the system.
Unlike static lookups that use the `map` property, dynamic lookups can reference large datasets
or frequently changing information without requiring constant updates to the integration.

**Implementation details**

The LookupCache resource referenced by this ID contains:
- The data records to be used as a reference source
- Configuration for how the data should be indexed and accessed
- Caching parameters to balance performance with data freshness

**Usage patterns**

Commonly used to reference:
- Product catalogs or SKU databases
- Customer or account information
- Pricing tables or discount rules
- Complex business logic lookup tables

Format: 24-character hexadecimal string (MongoDB ObjectId)

extract.description:
JSON path expression that extracts a specific value from the cached lookup object.

**Purpose**

When using dynamic lookups with a LookupCache, this JSON path identifies which field to extract
from the cached object after it has been retrieved using the lookup key.

**Implementation details**

- Must use JSON path syntax (similar to mapping extract fields)
- Operates on the cached object returned by the lookup operation
- Examples:
  - "$.name" - Extract the name field from the top level
  - "$.details.price" - Extract a nested price field
  - "$.attributes[0].value" - Extract a value from the first element of an array

**Usage scenario**

When a lookup cache contains complex objects:
```json
// Cache entry for key "PROD-123":
{
  "id": "PROD-123",
  "name": "Premium Widget",
  "details": {
    "price": 99.99,
    "currency": "USD",
    "inStock": true
  }
}
```

Setting extract to "$.details.price" would return 99.99 as the lookup result.

If no extract is provided, the entire cached object is returned as the lookup result.

default.description:
Default value to use when the source value is not found in the lookup map.
The platform stores `null` here when no default is configured.

This value is used as a fallback when:
1. The source value doesn't match any key in the map
2. allowFailures is set to true

Setting an appropriate default helps prevent flow failures due to unexpected
values and provides predictable behavior for edge cases.

Common default patterns include:
- Descriptive unknowns: "Unknown Country", "Unspecified Status"
- Original value indicators: "{Original Value}", "No mapping found"
- Neutral values: "Other", "N/A", "Miscellaneous"

If allowFailures is false and no default is specified, the flow will fail
when encountering unmapped values.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Omit this field entirely when no fallback value is intended. The API rejects an empty string with [invalid_field] Invalid value '' for field 'default' — emitting default: "" to mean "no default" fails validation; leaving the key out is the valid spelling of that intent.

allowFailures.description:
When true, missing lookup values will use the default value rather than causing an error.

**Behavior control**

This field determines how the system handles source values that don't exist in the map:

- true: Use the default value for missing mappings and continue processing
- false: Treat missing mappings as errors, failing the record

**Recommendation**

Set this to true when:
- New source values might appear over time
- Data quality issues could introduce unexpected values
- Processing should continue even with imperfect mapping

Set this to false when:
- Complete data accuracy is critical
- All possible source values are known and controlled
- Missing mappings indicate serious data problems that should be addressed

The best practice is typically to set allowFailures to true with a meaningful
default value, so flows remain operational while alerting you to missing mappings.

query.description:
SQL statements to execute; required when queryType is `["per_record"]`, `["per_page"]`, or `["first_page"]`, and typically contains a single statement.
Each element is a complete SQL statement as a plain string — never a single bare string and never an array of objects (objects cause a Cast error).
Inject values from the incoming record with Handlebars using the `record.` prefix and triple braces, e.g. `'{{{record.name}}}'` for strings (single-quoted in the SQL) and `{{{record.quantity}}}` for numbers.
Rendering is strict: a reference the render model cannot resolve (a bare `{{name}}` without prefix, or `record.*` when the arriving record is a grouped array) fails the step with `cannot_evaluate_handlebars` — it does not render an empty value.
`record` and `rows` are aliases chosen by the arriving data's shape: an object record binds `record` (`rows` undefined); a grouped array-record (e.g. upstream `groupByFields`) binds `rows` (`record` undefined) — address grouped rows as `{{rows.0.field}}` or iterate `{{#each rows}}`.
Double braces (`{{record.field}}`) output the value wrapped in single quotes with embedded quotes doubled, while triple braces output it raw; block helpers such as `{{#each}}` and `{{#if}}` use double braces as normal.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Use Handlebars to inject values from incoming records.
RDBMS queries REQUIRE the `record.` prefix on every field substitution.

## FORMAT — ARRAY OF STRINGS
This field is an ARRAY OF STRINGS, not a single string and not an array of objects.
- CORRECT: ["INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ({{record.name}}, {{record.email}})"]
- WRONG: "INSERT INTO users ..."  (not an array)
- WRONG: [{"query": "INSERT INTO users ..."}]  (objects are invalid — causes Cast error)
- WRONG: ["INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('{{name}}')"]  (missing record. prefix — rendering is strict, so the step fails with cannot_evaluate_handlebars)

## RDBMS HANDLEBARS SYNTAX

- **MUST use `record.` prefix** on per-record field references:
  `{{record.fieldName}}` or `{{{record.fieldName}}}`, NOT
  `{{fieldName}}` — an unprefixed reference is undefined in the
  render model and fails the step (strict rendering).
- **Grouped input binds `rows`, not `record`.** When the arriving
  record is a grouped array (upstream `groupByFields` or grouped
  file rows), `record` is undefined and the step fails; reference
  `{{rows.0.fieldName}}` or iterate `{{#each rows}}` instead. The
  two names are shape-dependent aliases over the same data.

- **Double-brace `{{record.field}}` vs. triple-brace `{{{record.field}}}`
  is a QUOTING CHOICE, not a syntax rule.** In RDBMS context the
  platform's Handlebars renderer treats double-brace specially: it
  auto-wraps the value as a SQL string literal (single-quoted, with
  embedded quotes escaped).  Triple-brace emits the raw value with
  no quoting.

  - `{{record.name}}`    →  `'Alice'` (auto-single-quoted, embedded `'` doubled to `''`)
  - `{{{record.name}}}`  →  `Alice`   (raw, no quoting — you must add your own)
  - `{{record.qty}}`     →  `'5'`     (numbers are also string-wrapped under double-brace)
  - `{{{record.qty}}}`   →  `5`       (numeric literal — what you usually want for INT columns)

  Pick by what the SQL needs at that slot:

  | Slot type                                | Use                       |
  |------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
  | String column value                      | `{{record.field}}`      |
  | Numeric column value (INT, DECIMAL, ...) | `{{{record.field}}}`    |
  | Stored procedure raw arg (already typed) | `{{{record.field}}}`    |
  | Identifier (table/column name)           | `{{{record.field}}}`    |
  | JSON literal (`PARSE_JSON`/JSONB)      | `{{{jsonSerialize record.subobject}}}` |

- **Block helpers** (`{{#each}}`, `{{#if}}`, `{{/each}}`,
  `{{#unless}}`) use double braces as normal — they emit no value.
- **Nested fields**: `{{record.properties.email}}` (auto-quoted)
  or `{{{record.properties.email}}}` (raw).

## EXAMPLES (production-grounded)

- INSERT (string columns, auto-quoted): `["INSERT INTO customers (name, email) VALUES ({{record.name}}, {{record.email}})"]`
- INSERT (mixed numeric + string): `["INSERT INTO orders (qty, sku) VALUES ({{{record.qty}}}, {{record.sku}})"]`
- UPDATE (numeric SET, string WHERE): `["UPDATE inventory SET qty = {{{record.qty}}} WHERE sku = {{record.sku}}"]`
- UPSERT (MySQL): `["INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES ({{{record.id}}}, {{record.name}}) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE name = {{record.name}}"]`
- MERGE (Snowflake): `["MERGE INTO target USING (SELECT {{record.email}} AS email) AS src ON target.email = src.email WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET name = {{record.name}}"]`
- Stored procedure (raw args): `["call netsuite.transformation_data_import({{record.record_type}}, 20)"]`
- JSON literal column (Snowflake VARIANT): `["INSERT INTO events (payload) SELECT PARSE_JSON({{jsonSerialize record.financialEvents}})"]`
- Per-page batch (different Handlebars context — see `queryType: per_page` below): `["{{#each batch_of_records}}UPDATE staging SET done=1 WHERE id={{{this.record.id}}};{{/each}}"]`
